questions.q: What does fujur, the root of the name Al-Fijar, mean?
questions.explain: The war was named "wicked" because it was fought in violation of the sacred months and sanctuary.

options: Four months in which fighting or bloodshed is forbidden
questions.explain: The four sacred months are Muharram, Rajab, Dhul-Qa'dah and Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.q: Who was killed in the dispute over the trade contract to Ukaz market?
questions.explain: Al-Barrat killed Urwah after losing the trading contract.

questions.q: How did the Fijar War end?
options: The Prophet SAW stopped it with arms
Quraysh offered diyah after about five years
questions.explain: Negotiation and diyah ended the war.

questions.q: In whose house was the Hilf Al-Fudul sealed?
questions.explain: The Hilf Al-Fudul was a pact to defend the wronged.

questions.q: Who cheated the Yemeni merchant and refused to pay?
questions.explain: The merchant complained publicly through poetry on Mount Abi Qubays.

questions.q: Trading during the Hajj season is permitted.
questions.explain: True. Al-Baqarah 2:198 says there is no blame in seeking the bounty of your Lord.

questions.q: Supporting your own side without judging right or wrong is a jahili mentality.
Put these events in the right order.

items.text: The pact to defend the wronged is sealed
The Yemeni merchant complains in verse
War breaks out in the sacred month and sanctuary

questions.explain: Urwah was killed, war broke out in the sacred month, diyah ended it, the merchant complained, and the pact was sealed.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: Compensation for a life or an injury

questions.explain: Fujur is wickedness, diyah is compensation, asabiyyah is tribal fanaticism and the red camel is a figure for precious wealth.

questions.q: What is the weakest level of faith when seeing wrongdoing?
questions.explain: The hadith mentions changing it by hand, by tongue, and finally in the heart.
